title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Site Ops and Top Support Issues (2026-03-04)
author: Maya Chen
content:
## Summary
This document defines standards and operating procedures for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, canonical API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the top support issues / canonical fixes we ship to reduce tickets. The goal is to keep docs predictable, reviewable, and directly actionable for engineers integrating Redwood Inference APIs.

## Scope
Applies to: eng-developer-experience team authors, SDK owners (python/js/go), Developer Relations, and Support triage engineers. Excludes experimental drafts stored in Google Drive.

## Owner and Roles
- Document owner: Maya Chen (DevEx)
- Reviewers: DevEx tech writers, SDK owners, Support engineering
- Maintainers: SDK owners for code examples; DevEx for site-level templates and joinery.

## High-level conventions (authoring)
1. Write for an engineer who knows HTTP and basic LLM concepts but not Redwood internals.
2. Use short descriptive file names: kebab-case, include year and month if significant. Example: `devex-sdk-quickstart-python-2026-03.json`.
3. Use sections: Overview, Quickstart (5-min), Full example (copy/paste), Troubleshooting, Best practices, Changelog.
4. Include ownership, SLOs for content (see below), and related pages.

## Content SLOs and publishing cadence
- Target: average of 2 reviewers, 95% of code samples executed and linted by CI.
- Update frequency: SDK guides: quarterly (or with breaking API change); Quickstarts: with SDK minor releases; Top issues: monthly.

## Docs site operating procedures
1. When publishing a new quickstart: create page -> attach runnable example snippet -> run docs-ci checks -> add code-sample tests -> assign reviewer -> publish.
2. Post-publish checklist: add to release-notes, create support playbook entry if this quickstart is likely to generate questions, add canonical tags and labels.
3. Emergency rollback: revert page and post a banner indicating the rollback reason + link to incident ticket.

## SDK guides and templates (required sections)
- Title, short description (1 line)
- Prerequisites (account, API key, region)
- Minimal quickstart (copy/paste to get a response in < 5 minutes)
- Full example: common patterns (streaming, tool-calls, batching, embeddings)
- Error cases & canonical fixes
- API compatibility matrix and SDK version table
- Ownership and contact

## Canonical API examples (format & placement)
- Keep examples concise (<= 40 LOC for minimal examples).
- Include Python and JavaScript versions for all generation and embedding flows.
- Tag examples with SDK version and a checksum so CI can detect drift.
- Store long-run integrative examples in a repo and link from the page.

## Top support issues and canonical fixes (current list)
| Issue | Root cause | Canonical fix / KB link | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Token-limit errors in streaming | Clients assume unlimited context; models enforce seq-len | Validate prompt length client-side; fallback to chunking + summarization. KB: /kb/token-limit-errors | Support Eng |
| 401/invalid-api-key | Key rotation / wrong env var name | Standardize env var names (REDWOOD_API_KEY); add startup-time validation | SDK owners |
| Slow cold-start on dedicated pools | Model not pinned or cold kernel path | Recommend pinning model-version and warmup endpoint (see warmup playbook) | Eng Platform |
| Inconsistent embeddings similarity scores | Mixed model versions across calls | Enforce model version pin; add matrix tests in CI | Applied ML |
| Excessive token usage (unexpected costs) | Prompt engineering + missing token-count guardrails | Add token-budgeting examples; instrument token estimators in snippets | DevEx / Product |

Each row links to a canonical KB article and a runnable example. When a fix is applied, update the quickstart and mark the support ticket resolved with link to the doc.

## Troubleshooting flow (triage)
1. Reproduce with minimal example (documented example preferred).
2. Confirm SDK version and model-version.
3. Capture request/response (obscure PII).
4. Check platform dashboards (latency, error rates) and recent deploys.
5. If fix is generic, update canonical fix and quickstart; if scoped, escalate to owner.

## Templates (copy/paste)
- Minimal quickstart header:

Title: <Short title>
Description: <1-line>
Prereqs: API key, SDK version x.y.z
Quickstart (python):
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
print(client.generate("Write a 2-line haiku about clouds."))
```

- Issue report template for docs and support:
Summary: (1 line)
Steps to reproduce:
Expected result:
Actual result:
Suggested canonical fix:
CI tests to add:

## Code sample CI and linting
- All code snippets on docs pages must be covered by docs-ci: a minimalist test that runs the snippet with sandboxed key and asserts output shape. Failures block publish.
- Snippet metadata must include: language, sdk-version, test-runner-id.

## Ownership and review process
- New page: author -> 2 reviewers -> devex-prod owner approves -> publish.
- Major edits: add changelog entry and notify support and SDK owners.

## Operational metrics (tracked)
- Number of support tickets opened per quickstart (target < 2/month per popular quickstart).
- Percentage of published snippets covered by CI (target 95%).
- Mean time to update canonical fix after a support triage (target < 7 days).

## Example canonical-fix entry (full)
Title: Fix for 401s when using environment variable REDWOOD_API_KEY
Summary: Users were getting 401s due to inconsistent env variable names and missing startup validation.
Fix steps:
1. Standardize env var name in all quickstarts to REDWOOD_API_KEY.
2. Add startup validation code to SDKs that emits a clear error when the key is missing or malformed.
3. Add CI snippet that runs startup validation on publish.
4. Update quickstarts and create KB article.
Owner: SDK owners
